about: Experimental typed-IR spike mutants (wf10 IR1, owner q128). Each test kills one mutant of this repository that no other test kills. Every killer needs the two toolchains (ERGO_IRSPIKE_GOROOT_SOURCE, ERGO_IRSPIKE_GOROOT_IR: the go1.27.0 derivative at /home/exedev/Developer/personal/.worktrees/go-irspike, and ERGO_IRSPIKE_CACHE) and builds Go (full tier); without them the tests skip and every row survives, so run the ledger with the toolchains set. The derivative's own mutants live outside this repository and are recorded here by name only (go-irspike, wf10 IR1 round 1): M1 the decoder swaps binary operands, M2 drops the else branch, M4 the IR path builds with bounds checks off (-B), all killed by TestIRMatchesSource; M6 the decoder accepts a type mismatch, killed by TestIRBodyThatDoesNotCheck. TestIRRuntimeChecks (race detector, GC checkmark) was deleted in batch-18 fix-tool: it guarded only the derivative's stack and pointer maps, and no mutant of this repository reached it.

mutants.name: irspike-unary-dropped
mutants.from: return &irExpr{K: "un", Pos: p, Op: op, X: b.expr(x.X)}
mutants.rule: An IR unary expression keeps its operator (! and -): the IR path prints what the source path prints. Only the generated programs hold a unary operator; the kernel has none.

mutants.name: irspike-ir-line-shifted
mutants.rule: An IR node carries its .ergo line, so the derivative reports an IR body that does not check at the source position.

mutants.name: irspike-ir-name-not-content
mutants.origin: wf10 batch-18 fix-tool (verify M2, the IR1 request's M5)
mutants.rule: The -ergoir flag, the one key of the IR in Go's build cache, names the IR file's content, not the module it was written in: an edit of the IR alone, in the same module, builds again (each seed of TestIRMatchesSource writes its own module, so only this test sees the difference).
